answer: Before an agent may sell steam service, the boiler inspector checks the National Board number stamped on each pressure vessel against the national registry and the inspection certificate posted in the room. One stamp number on two vessels trips a red tag shutdown, an insurer cancellation and a call on the installer surety bond. A vessel costs 1800, the hydrostatic test 480 and the inspection 220, so N fakes cost N x 2500 and each still needs a fired boiler in a real plant with fuel and an operator. A pigment works on the ridge above the wharf cannot hide a second vessel under one stamp.
